n: The fifth and final vision: the Lord stands by the altar and orders the shrine’s pillars struck so the building collapses on the worshipers. No one will escape.

f.g: Probably the altar at Bethel, the center of Israel’s false worship.
The capital or top of a pillar.

n: There is nowhere to hide from God — not the depths of the earth or the heights of heaven. A dark reversal of Psalm 139’s comfort.

f.g: Hebrew Sheol — the world of the dead, imagined as deep below.

f.w: though they climb up to heaven

n: Not the forests on top of Mount Carmel or the bottom of the sea will hide them; God commands even the sea serpent.

f.g: A wooded, cave-filled ridge — a natural hiding place.
A sea monster; God controls even the chaos creatures of the deep.

n: Even in exile they will not be safe. God will watch them “for evil, and not for good” — the opposite of His usual protective care.

f.w: I will set mine eyes upon them

n: Another hymn of God’s power: He touches the earth and it melts; the land heaves like the Nile.

f.w: as by the flood of Egypt

n: He builds His upper rooms in the heavens and sets the sky’s vault over the earth; He pours out the seas. The Lord is His name.
A startling question: Are you any different to Me than the Ethiopians? I guided other peoples’ migrations too. Being chosen does not make Israel immune to judgment.

f.g: Cushites, from the far south along the Nile — a distant people.
Probably Crete, the Philistines’ place of origin.

n: The sinful kingdom will be destroyed — but not completely. A remnant of Jacob’s house will survive. Hope begins to dawn.

f.w: I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob

n: Israel will be scattered among all nations as grain is shaken in a sieve — yet not a single grain will be lost. God keeps track of every scattered Israelite, the basis for the promised gathering.

f.w: I will sift the house of Israel among all nations
yet shall not the least grain fall upon the earth

n: The sinners who said, “Disaster won’t touch us,” will die. Overconfidence is no protection.
Restoration! God will rebuild David’s fallen “booth.” James quoted this at the Jerusalem council, applying it to Gentiles joining the Church through Christ, the Son of David.

f.g: Booth or hut — David’s dynasty, now a fallen shelter.

f.w: In that day will I raise up the tabernacle of David

n: Restored Israel will possess what remains of Edom and of all nations called by the Lord’s name. The Greek version read “that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord,” the form James quoted.

f.w: which are called by my name

n: Harvests will be so abundant that plowing season overtakes reaping, and grape-treading runs into sowing. Mountains will drip with sweet wine — a picture of millennial plenty.

f.w: the plowman shall overtake the reaper
the mountains shall drop sweet wine

n: God will bring His people back. They will rebuild ruined cities and actually enjoy their vineyards and gardens — reversing the curses of Amos 5:11.

f.g: Restore the fortunes; bring back the exiles.

n: The book ends with a promise: God will plant Israel in their land, never to be uprooted again. Judgment is not God’s last word — restoration is.

f.w: I will plant them upon their land
